question.text: Under the standard (pledgor-initiated) closure of a pledge or hypothecation after the pledgor has repaid the loan, as described on pages 170 and 174 of the NISM Series-VI (September 2025) workbook, who initiates the closure (unpledge) request?

answer.text: The pledgor, through its DP, initiates the closure and the pledgee confirms it through its DP
The pledgee unilaterally, without any input from the pledgor
The depository, automatically on receipt of the loan repayment
The issuer of the underlying securities, through a corporate-action style instruction

explanation.text: The Logic: Pages 170 and 174 of NISM Series-VI (September 2025) describe the standard closure process after loan repayment as being initiated by the pledgor through its DP, with the pledgee then confirming the closure through its DP. The stem now restricts the question to that standard pledgor-initiated scenario, making this answer unique. The Trap: The depository does not act automatically, and the issuer of the underlying securities has no role in pledge closure. The audit flagged the original because page 176 of the same workbook separately describes a unilateral closure by the pledgee, so "either party" or "the pledgee" was defensible without narrowing the stem. Note: The original was ambiguous because page 176 also provides for unilateral pledgee-initiated closure, making "either party" or "pledgee" defensible. The stem is now restricted to the standard pledgor-initiated post-repayment closure on pp.170 and 174, uniquely supporting "the pledgor through its DP".
